mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from its deep trough at t-1w to t-0w indicates a strong return to regular commuting patterns, which will directly translate into increased foot traffic and spending at retail and recreation venues during weekdays over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining above its t-2w level for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in PARKS mobility from t-1w to t-0w, following a brief surge, suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure activities. This redirection of leisure time and spending is expected to boost indoor retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next two weeks, or if PARKS mobility rebounds significantly, invalidating the premise of diverted leisure activity.

mechanism_narrative: The clear inverse movement between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility in the latest week (WORKPLACES up, RESIDENTIAL down) signifies a broad shift from home-based activities to out-of-home engagement. This fundamental change in daily routines will drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, or if WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility do not maintain their inverse relationship for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite fluctuations in other categories, RETAIL_REC has consistently remained significantly below its baseline, indicating persistent underlying consumer caution or economic constraints. This sustained low level suggests that discretionary spending will continue to be suppressed, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, or if RETAIL_REC rises above -10% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The substantial week-on-week increase in TRANSIT station mobility from t-1w to t-0w signals a renewed willingness and necessity for people to travel, particularly for commuting. This increased movement directly facilitates greater access to and engagement with retail and recreation venues in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next week, or if TRANSIT mobility falls back below its t-1w level in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The relative stability of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, representing essential spending, contrasted with the recent sharp dip in RETAIL_REC, indicates that consumers are prioritizing necessities while pulling back on discretionary retail and recreation. This pattern suggests continued pressure on non-essential spending, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase (more than 5 percentage points) in either of the next two weeks, while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable or declines.

mechanism_narrative: As the metropolitan area enters the late spring period, the natural inclination towards outdoor activities, particularly in parks, tends to increase. This seasonal shift in leisure preference often diverts foot traffic and spending away from indoor retail and recreation, leading to a slight decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility consistently remains below its t-0w level for the next four weeks, or if RETAIL_REC shows a sustained increase over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: While WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility have shown a strong rebound from their t-1w lows, the concurrent decline in RETAIL_REC at t-0w suggests a decoupling effect. This indicates that increased commuting does not automatically translate to increased discretionary retail spending, implying persistent behavioral shifts that will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC falls
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT maintaining their rebound.
